```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", error = FALSE)
library(readfiscalau)
source("_helpers.R")
```

`readfiscalau` gives applications two complementary catalogue layers for
finding and selecting fiscal resources:

- discovery parses a current official HTML/CKAN response into candidate or
  resource rows; and
- the bundled manifest and coverage panels identify releases and schemas that
  have been curated, hash-bound, and admitted by the package contract.

Use discovery to find changed or newly published links, then use the manifest
and coverage panels to select a release that has a known schema and provenance
contract. A discovered row remains a candidate until it is admitted to the
manifest; this keeps selection and parsing decisions explicit.

## HTML release discovery

This packaged HTML snapshot is an offline replay fixture shaped like an
official Treasury downloads page. It contains Budget, MYEFO, and FBO links.

```{r html-discovery}
html_candidates <- discover_au_fiscal_releases(
  source = "treasury",
  raw = example_raw("treasury-downloads.html")
)
html_candidates[, c(
  "source_id", "release_type", "title", "fiscal_year",
  "resource_url", "discovery_status"
)]
```

Each row is a candidate. `discovery_status = "needs_metadata"` is possible
when the page provides no fiscal year; such a row is not silently promoted to
a readable release. Finance discovery additionally rejects a June link that
is labelled as a monthly statement, because June is an annual FBO/CFS boundary.

The live equivalent supplies an official URL and omits `raw`; the package then
uses the bounded HTTPS transport and cache:

```r
live_candidates <- discover_au_fiscal_releases(source = "treasury")
```

The live call is shown for orientation only. CRAN vignette builds use the
offline fixture above, so rendering remains deterministic while the live path
stays visible to application authors.

## Finance CKAN resource discovery

The CKAN helper keeps all resource vintages in a successful `package_show`
payload. This is important for overwrite-in-place workbooks, where the update
timestamp is part of the release identity.

```{r ckan-discovery}
ckan_resources <- discover_finance_ckan_resources(
  raw = example_raw("finance-ckan.json")
)
ckan_resources[, c(
  "resource_id", "name", "format", "created", "last_modified",
  "resource_url", "license"
)]
```

The returned rows are metadata, not parsed observations. Select an admitted
manifest row before calling a reader.

## Curated manifest and coverage

The manifest has one row per publication/resource vintage. Filter by source and
release type to see what the installed package knows:

```{r manifest}
manifest <- list_au_fiscal_releases(source = "all")
as.data.frame(table(manifest$source_id, manifest$release_type))
```

For Budget and MYEFO, use the coverage panels to select an exact table family,
series, status, date range, unit, and accounting basis without fetching a
document:

```{r coverage}
budget_series <- list_au_budget_series()
budget_series[budget_series$series == "Total receipts",
              c("release_id", "table_family", "series",
                "actual_forecast", "start_date", "end_date",
                "unit", "accounting_basis", "observation_source_url",
                "observation_source_sha256")][1:6, ]
```

`list_au_pbo_historical_tables()` and
`list_au_pbo_historical_series()` provide the corresponding table-oriented
catalogue for the PBO workbook. `list_au_fiscal_search_controls()` is a cheaper
projection for an application search panel and intentionally does not load
series-level coverage.

### Read the source terms at the right level

The release manifest’s `license`, `terms_url`, and `attribution` describe the
selected release/resource. The coverage rows above add an observation-level
source URL and SHA-256. This distinction matters because some Budget and MYEFO
table families use the PBO structured products
[*Historical budget forecasts and measures*](https://www.pbo.gov.au/copyright-information)
for normalisation while retaining the Treasury release identity. A PBO
`observation_source_url` is subject to the PBO copyright notice and its CC
BY-NC-ND 4.0 International caveat; the Treasury release terms do not license
those PBO-derived observations. Keep both hashes and consult `inst/TERMS.md`
before redistribution.

## Source boundaries

The admitted families include Treasury chart CSV/ZIP resources and curated
Budget/MYEFO snapshot panels, Finance aggregate workbooks, the FBO history DOCX,
and the PBO Historical Fiscal Data workbook. The package does not generally
parse arbitrary PDF, DOCX, workbook, HTML, appropriation-table, or
financial-statement-note content. Use discovery to record such URLs and the
typed readers for admitted families; a URL can remain a documented candidate
until a matching reader and schema contract are available.

## Build a reproducible workflow

Use `readfiscalau.Rmd` for the first offline read, and
`provenance-and-cache.Rmd` for exact-byte replay. Before a source change is
admitted, preserve its URL/hash/terms metadata, add a small fixture, and add a
contract test that records the intended schema and failure behavior.
